title: Read every existing dashboard end to end
why_matters: Every dashboard on the team's BI tool is a record of what the previous DAs thought mattered, what stakeholders asked for, and which questions never quite got answered. Most new DAs skim the dashboards; the ones who get respected in their first month read each one carefully — including the ones nobody uses anymore. By week four you'll be the person responsible for shipping new ones; by week one, you understand what's already there and where the gaps are.
steps: List every dashboard in the team's BI tool. There will be more than you think. Group them by owner, audience, and last-viewed date.

Open each dashboard. Don't just look at the charts — read the underlying SQL (or dbt models) where available. Note the patterns: who builds with CTEs, who uses self-joins, where the conventions break.

Identify the dashboards that haven't been viewed in 60+ days. Those are the abandoned ones. Note who requested them; the abandonment pattern often tells you which stakeholders 'want a dashboard' but never use one.
For each dashboard you couldn't immediately interpret in 10 seconds, note why. That note becomes your map of what 'good' looks like on this team — and what doesn't.
success_criteria: By end of week, you can list every dashboard, name its primary user, and name the 3-5 that have been abandoned and the 3-5 that are getting the most use. You can describe two stylistic conventions the team uses without checking the documentation.
reflection_prompt: Of the abandoned dashboards, which one looks like it was the right idea built badly — versus the wrong idea entirely? Two sentences.
